content.text: Automated feedback occupies a different position in the revision process. Zhang and Hyland (2018) found that automated writing evaluation tended to flag rather than correct errors, and that teacher feedback addressed more error types than the automated system, although differing assignment demands may have confounded the comparison. In an integrated classroom case study, the majority of 33 students actively engaged with combined automated, peer, and teacher feedback, and the approach promoted behavioural, affective, and cognitive engagement and encouraged thoughtful revisions (Zhang & Hyland, 2021). The same authors note that students were not required to address all feedback received (Zhang & Hyland, 2021).
